- **Enacting clause / purpose of Act**
  - Authorizes appropriations for FY2024 for: Department of Defense military activities; military construction; Department of Energy defense activities.
  - Prescribes FY2024 military personnel strengths.
  - Enacted as Public Law 118-31, H.R. 2670, Dec. 22, 2023.

- **Sec. 1 — Short title**
  - Act may be cited as **“National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024.”**
  - No appropriated/authorized dollar amount stated.
  - No amendment to existing law stated.

- **Sec. 2 — Organization of Act into divisions; table of contents**
  - Organizes Act into 7 divisions:
    - Division A — Department of Defense Authorizations.
    - Division B — Military Construction Authorizations.
    - Division C — Department of Energy National Security Authorizations and Other Authorizations.
    - Division D — Funding Tables.
    - Division E — Other Matters.
    - Division F — Department of State Authorization Act of 2023.
    - Division G — Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024.
  - Sets table of contents for all listed sections/titles/subtitles.
  - No dollar amounts stated in this section; no amendments to existing law stated.

- **Sec. 3 — Congressional defense committees**
  - Defines “congressional defense committees” for the Act by cross-reference to **10 U.S.C. 101(a)(16)**.
  - Codified note reference shown: **10 U.S.C. 101 note**.
  - No funding amount; no substantive amendment text included.

- **Sec. 4 — Budgetary effects of this Act**
  - For compliance with the **Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010**, budgetary effects are determined by reference to the latest statement titled **“Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation”** for this Act.
  - Condition: statement must be jointly submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairmen of the House and Senate Budget Committees.
  - Further condition: statement must be submitted before the vote on passage in the House acting first on the conference report or amendment between the Houses.
  - No dollar amount stated in the text.

- **Sec. 101 — Authorization of appropriations**
  - Authorizes FY2024 appropriations for procurement for: Army; Navy and Marine Corps; Air Force and Space Force; Defense-wide activities.
  - Mechanism: amounts are “as specified in the funding table in section 4101.”
  - No exact dollar figures appear in this text.

- **Sec. 111 — Limitation pending assessment of Army Trackless Moving Target systems**
  - Applies to FY2024 funds authorized by this Act or otherwise made available for the Army **Trackless Moving Target program**.
  - Funding limitation: not more than **75 percent** may be obligated or expended to procure or further develop the **Trackless Moving Target–Infantry variant** until required actions occur.
  - Preconditions:
    - Secretary of the Army, through Army Combat Capabilities Development Command, conducts assessment including end-user feedback and comparison against applicable requirements in March 2023 report **“Autonomous Robotic Targets for Small Arms Range Training.”**
    - Secretary obtains direct soldier feedback on current program.
    - Secretary certifies to congressional defense committees that Army acquisition strategy for the Infantry variant meets program requirements in that March 2023 report.
    - Secretary submits required report.
  - Report deadline: not later than **30 days after completion** of the assessment and soldier feedback.
  - Report must include assessment results, comparison to other operationally deployed commercially available targets used by other Armed Forces, summary of soldier feedback, and certification of compliance with **10 U.S.C. 4061**.

- **Sec. 123—Virginia class submarine multiyear procurement**
  - Navy Secretary may, subject to **10 U.S.C. 3501**, enter multiyear contracts for procurement of **not more than 13 Virginia class submarines**.
  - May enter advance-procurement contracts **beginning FY2024** for covered submarines and associated equipment/subsystems, including long-lead material and economic order quantities where cost savings are achievable.
  - Post-FY2025 payments subject to availability of appropriations/funds.
  - Construction contracts must cap U.S. termination liability at amount appropriated for covered submarines, regardless of amount obligated.
  - “Virginia class submarine” = **block VI configured** Virginia class submarine.

- **Sec. 124—Auxiliary Personnel Lighter**
  - Navy Secretary may, **beginning FY2024**, contract for up to **six Auxiliary Personnel Lighter class vessels** and associated material.
  - Payments subject to appropriations; termination liability limited to funding obligated at termination.

  - Adds **10 U.S.C. 986**: Secretary of Defense may neither require nor prohibit armed forces members or DoD civilian employees from identifying gender or personal pronouns in official DoD correspondence.

- **Sec. 523 — Foreign post-service employment**
  - Adds **10 U.S.C. 989**: covered individuals—retired/separated active or reserve members—may not occupy covered post-service positions involving national security/intelligence/military/internal security services for governments of “countries of concern” under **22 U.S.C. 2651a(m)**, proxy/pass-through countries as determined by SecDef, or controlled/financed entities.

  - Notifications to SASC/HASC due **30 days** after waiver/revocation; specified elements.
  - SecDef must create pre-separation written notice/certification process.
  - Penalties for knowing/willful violation: withhold DoD pay/allowances/benefits; revoke security clearance.

- **Sec. 1074—Holistic training range assessment**
  - Secretary of Defense, after coordinating with military department Secretaries, must assess capabilities, limitations, and anticipated future constraints on use of U.S./overseas military lands, marine areas, and airspace for Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force training.
  - Required contents: range capability by facility; current/future training requirements; regional interconnectivity opportunities; adequacy of DOD resources including virtual/constructive assets for fifth-generation weapons systems and near-peer competition; adversarial intelligence collection threats; electromagnetic warfare capacity; Joint All Domain operations capacity/shortfalls; theater-level operations vs. pacing threat under 10 U.S.C. 113(g), including Pacific Deterrence Initiative simulations; proposals with timelines/budget estimates to enhance capabilities/mitigate shortfalls or encroachment.
  - Initial report due with FY2026 President’s budget under 31 U.S.C. 1105. Annual follow-up reports due with FY2027–FY2032 budgets on implementation and actions addressing training constraints.

- **Sec. 1075—Special operations force structure**
  - Within 90 days: SecDef report to congressional defense committees assessing optimal SOF force structure; includes NDS role, geographic combatant command demand, general-purpose-force effects, headquarters structure, adequacy for National Military Strategy under 10 U.S.C. 153(b), Joint Concept for Competing role.
